# Monorepos routinely use `git sparse-checkout`, which turns on
# extensions.worktreeConfig in .git/config. sesam opens every repository through
# go-git, which refuses a repository carrying that extension - so all commands
# fail, and the hooks (which swallow the resolve error to stay out of git's
# way) degrade to a silent no-op: `git commit` then proceeds without sealing
# or verifying anything.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir app
cp appfile app/index.js
mkdir vault
exec sesam init --user admin --sesam-dir vault
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init monorepo with nested sesam'

# Narrow the checkout to the directories we care about; vault stays present.
exec git sparse-checkout set --cone vault app
exec git config extensions.worktreeConfig
stdout 'true'
exists vault/.sesam/audit/log.jsonl

# sesam must keep working in the sparse checkout.
exec sesam --sesam-dir vault status --all
stdout 'README\.md'

# Drift the secret: the pre-commit hook must seal it and stage the object, not
# skip silently because it could not open the repository.
cp changed vault/README.md
exec sesam --sesam-dir vault hook pre-commit
exec git diff --cached --name-only
stdout 'vault/\.sesam/objects/README\.md\.sesam'

-- appfile --
console.log(1)
-- changed --
# changed readme
